quick.summary: Stop support requests by building standard tools that are too easy to ignore.
quick.takeaway: Build the easy road, and people will naturally follow it safely.

beats.line: Engineers keep asking me to fix their broken pipelines. How do I stop this?
Think of a park. People always walk across the grass to save time.
Right, and they leave an ugly trail of mud behind them.
So you build a smooth stone path exactly where they want to walk.
Make the easiest way the safest way?
Yes. We call this the golden path.
Can I just say the easy road?
I like that. The easy road. Give them tools that just work automatically.
So if they use my road, they never need to ask for directions.
Exactly. And your support tickets will disappear.

quiz.question: What does it mean to build the easy road?
options: Creating safe tools that are the fastest way to work.
Writing a long manual about how to code perfectly.
Locking out everyone who makes a mistake.
Telling engineers to figure out their own problems.
quiz.explanation: The goal is to make the correct, safe way to build things also the easiest way to do it.

quiz.question: Engineers will ignore a tool if the old, messy way is still faster.
quiz.explanation: People will always look for a shortcut. The safe tools you build must save them time, or they will not use them.
